errors.meaning: Execution reached a NEXT while no FOR loop it could close was open.

A line could not be read as a statement: it names nothing the interpreter recognises as a command, or the text around a command does not fit the form that command takes. A READ whose DATA item cannot be held by the variable it is read into raises this too.
Execution reached a RETURN with no GOSUB call outstanding to return from.
A READ was executed with every DATA item in the program already consumed.
A statement or built-in function was given an argument outside the domain it accepts, or was asked for a result outside the range it can produce.
A value went past what its numeric type can hold, whether it was computed by an operation or supplied to the program as input.
BASIC's workspace ran out: program text, variable and array storage, and the stack that open loops and subroutine calls occupy all draw on it.
A transfer of control named a line number the program does not contain.
An array subscript fell outside the array's bounds — those fixed by DIM, or, for an array used without a DIM, the implicit upper bound of 10, counted from the origin OPTION BASE sets.
DIM was applied to an array that already has dimensions, whether an earlier DIM or the array's first use fixed them.
An expression asked for a quantity that is not finite — a divisor of zero, or zero raised to a negative power — so no representable value can be produced.
A statement valid only inside a stored program was entered in direct mode.
A value's type does not agree with the position it is used in: a string where a number is expected, or a number where a string is.
The strings a program holds at once outgrew the memory set aside for string storage.
A single string value was made longer than 255 bytes.
A string expression is beyond the complexity the interpreter will evaluate.
CONT could not resume a halted program, because the program text was altered while it was stopped.
A call named a user-defined function no DEF FN has defined, or a machine-code entry point no DEF USR has defined.
Control ran off the end of an error-handling routine without a statement that ends error handling, leaving execution nowhere to continue.
RESUME was executed while no error was being handled.
An error code the interpreter prints under a shared placeholder rather than a message of its own. ERROR can raise such a code, which leaves it free for a program's own error conditions.
errors.note: The manual heads this entry with the codes 21, 24, 25, and 28 followed by 他 — "and others". Further codes share this message and are not listed, so the set of unprintable codes, and with it the set of error codes as a whole, is larger than what is recorded here.

An input line was longer than the 255 bytes a line may occupy.

A read from cassette tape failed.

errors.meaning: A WHILE loop was left open, with no WEND anywhere that closes it.
Execution reached a WEND with no WHILE loop it could close open.
The same label name is attached to more than one line of the program.
A statement branched to a label name the program never defines.
A statement was executed that this machine, as currently equipped and configured, cannot carry out.
The fields FIELD lays over a random-access record total more than 255 bytes.
A file number was used that is above the count of files the system is configured to hold open at once.
A file operation named a file that is not present on the disk.
An operation needing sole use of a file was applied to one that is already open.
A read from a file was attempted with no data left beyond the point already reached.
A file operation was given a name that is not a well-formed file name.
Loading a program stored in ASCII form found a line carrying no line number.
A file opened for sequential access was given an operation only random access supports; MERGE reading a program saved in binary rather than ASCII form raises it too.
A statement referred to a file number with no open file behind it.
A write was directed at a file, disk, or drive marked as not writable — by a protection attribute, or by the write-protect tab on the medium itself.
A file operation addressed a drive with no disk loaded in it.
A transfer to or from the disk did not complete.
NAME was asked to give a file a name another file on the disk already holds.
A write to disk found no free space left to write into.
The allocation table on the disk is damaged, leaving the layout of its files unreadable.
A file operation's drive specification does not name a drive this system can use.
A direct sector transfer was given a head, track, or sector number the disk does not have.
NAME was asked to rename a file across drives; the old and new names must land on the same disk.
Insert-mode key entry on the scroll window's first line had nowhere to push the text already in the window, the window being full.
